quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "An airport departures board flickering with a full page of flights"?
quests.hint: Think about when airports are usually busiest with departing flights.
quests.explanation: Yes! Airports are usually busiest with flights during the day.
quests.funFact: Some of the world's busiest airports handle over a thousand flights every single day!

quests.instruction: "An airport departures board glowing quietly with just a few late flights" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when an airport would be quiet, with only a few flights left.
quests.explanation: Yes! A quiet airport with just a few late flights suggests it's nighttime.
quests.funFact: Some flights are scheduled overnight specifically so passengers arrive fresh in the morning!

quests.instruction: "A crossing guard's shadow stretching long across the crosswalk in the early hours" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when shadows are longest, even though the sun is already up.
quests.explanation: Yes! Early morning is part of the daytime, even though the low sun makes shadows extra long.
quests.funFact: Shadows are longest right after sunrise and right before sunset!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A shadow completely gone, swallowed up by the dark street"?
quests.hint: Think about what a street would look like with absolutely no sunlight left.
quests.explanation: Yes! A shadow disappearing completely happens once the sun has set, at night.
quests.funFact: Shadows can only form when there's a bright light source, like the sun, to cast them!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A ferry horn sounding as it docks, sunlight sparkling on the water". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what's making the water sparkle so brightly.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sunlight sparkling on the water tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Ferry horns are used to warn other boats and let passengers know the ferry is arriving!

quests.instruction: "A ferry horn echoing across still, black water" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'black' describing the water — when does water look like that?
quests.explanation: Yes! Black water tells you it's nighttime, with no sunlight to light it up.
quests.funFact: Sound can actually travel especially clearly across calm water at night!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A subway platform crowded with commuters checking their watches". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when subway platforms are usually most crowded.
quests.explanation: Yes! Subway platforms are usually most crowded during the day, especially on the way to work.
quests.funFact: Some subway systems carry millions of passengers underground every single day!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A subway platform nearly empty except for one yawning rider". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when a usually busy subway platform would be nearly empty.
quests.explanation: Yes! A nearly empty subway platform suggests it's very late at night.
quests.funFact: Some subway systems run all night long, though with far fewer trains than during the day!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A weather balloon released to gather data as the sky brightens"?
quests.hint: Think about what 'as the sky brightens' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! A brightening sky tells you the day is beginning.
quests.funFact: Weather balloons can rise over 20 miles high before they finally burst!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A weather balloon's tracking light blinking as it drifts unseen overhead"?
quests.hint: Think about why a balloon would need a blinking light to be tracked at all.
quests.explanation: Yes! A blinking tracking light is most useful once it's too dark to see the balloon itself.
quests.funFact: Some weather balloons are launched at night to gather data on overnight weather changes!

quests.instruction: "A farmers cooperative auctioning fresh produce under an open-air tent" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a fresh produce auction would usually be held.
quests.explanation: Yes! Fresh produce auctions are usually held during the day.
quests.funFact: Farmers often sell their crops together at auctions to reach more buyers at once!

quests.instruction: "A farmers cooperative's gates chained shut, the auction long over" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a busy auction site would finally be closed and locked.
quests.explanation: Yes! Chained, locked gates after the auction suggest it's now night.
quests.funFact: Farm auctions can sometimes last for many hours, from morning into the afternoon!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A city bike-share station nearly emptied of its bikes by midday". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when a bike-share station would already be nearly emptied out.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bikes are usually borrowed most in the middle of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Bike-share programs let people borrow a bike for a short ride and return it at any station!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A city bike-share station glowing under a single lamp, mostly full again". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when a bike-share station would be lit by just a single lamp.
quests.explanation: Yes! A station lit by a single lamp suggests it's dark outside, at night.
quests.funFact: Bike-share stations fill back up in the evening as riders finish their commutes home!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A drone hobbyist testing a new flight pattern over a sunny field"?
quests.hint: Think about when it's easiest to see a small drone flying against the sky.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunny field tells you it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Drone pilots often practice during the day, when it's easiest to see the drone clearly!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A drone hobbyist packing up gear as fireflies begin to blink nearby"?
quests.hint: Think about when fireflies actually begin to blink and glow.
quests.explanation: Yes! Fireflies begin blinking once it starts getting dark, at night.
quests.funFact: Fireflies use their blinking light partly to find and attract a mate!

quests.instruction: "A window cleaner's bucket sloshing as he reaches the top floor" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when window washing is usually done, so it's easy to see the glass.
quests.explanation: Yes! Window cleaning is usually done during the day.
quests.funFact: Window washers use special safety harnesses to stay secure while working so high up!

quests.instruction: "A window cleaner's bucket long put away, the building dark and still" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a busy office building would finally be dark and still.
quests.explanation: Yes! A dark, still building suggests everyone has gone home for the night.
quests.funFact: Many office buildings dim their lights automatically once everyone has left!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A radio traffic report warning drivers about a busy commute". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when roads are usually busiest with commuting traffic.
quests.explanation: Yes! Roads are usually busiest with commuters during the day.
quests.funFact: Traffic reporters sometimes fly in helicopters to get a clear view of busy roads!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A radio host reading calm traffic updates to a nearly empty highway"?
quests.hint: Think about when a usually busy highway would become nearly empty.
quests.explanation: Yes! A nearly empty highway suggests it's late at night.
quests.funFact: Some radio stations play calm, quiet updates specifically for late-night drivers!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A hot air balloon festival launching dozens of balloons at once"?
quests.hint: Think about when hot air balloon festivals are usually held, so pilots can see clearly.
quests.explanation: Yes! Hot air balloon festivals are usually held during the day.
quests.funFact: Balloon festivals can have dozens of colorful balloons launching all at once!

quests.instruction: "A hot air balloon glow show, baskets lit up bright against the black sky" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'black sky' — when do we see a sky like that?
quests.explanation: Yes! A black sky tells you it's nighttime, perfect for a glowing balloon show.
quests.funFact: During a balloon glow show, pilots fire their burners together to light up the night sky!

quests.instruction: "A crowd gathering early for a museum's members-only preview hour" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when museums usually open their doors for visitors.
quests.explanation: Yes! Museums are usually open and welcoming visitors during the day.
quests.funFact: Some museums offer special early hours just for their members!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A museum's guards making rounds through silent, empty galleries"?
quests.hint: Think about when a museum would be closed, silent, and empty of visitors.
quests.explanation: Yes! A silent, empty museum suggests it's closed for the night.
quests.funFact: Museum guards help keep valuable art and artifacts safe, even after the doors close!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A tide chart showing the ocean pulling back to reveal a wide beach". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when families usually visit the beach to explore the tide pools.
quests.explanation: Yes! Beach visits to explore a low tide are usually a daytime activity.
quests.funFact: Tides happen because the moon's gravity pulls on Earth's oceans, whether it's day or night!

quests.instruction: "A tide chart marking the ocean creeping back in under a rising moon" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'rising moon' — when does the moon actually rise?
quests.explanation: Yes! A rising moon is visible at night.
quests.funFact: Tides happen because of the moon's gravity, pulling on Earth's oceans day and night!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A greenhouse mister spraying rows of seedlings under skylights"?
quests.hint: Think about when skylights would actually let in bright natural light.
quests.explanation: Yes! Skylights let in natural light during the day.
quests.funFact: Greenhouses trap warmth from sunlight to help plants grow even in cooler weather!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A greenhouse's misters resting, its glass reflecting only starlight"?
quests.hint: Think about the word 'starlight' — when is that actually visible?
quests.explanation: Yes! Starlight is only visible at night.
quests.funFact: Even at night, a greenhouse keeps working to trap warmth for its plants!

quests.instruction: "A parade float being adjusted just before the big march begins" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when most parades are held, so crowds can watch easily.
quests.explanation: Yes! Most parades are held during the day.
quests.funFact: Some parade floats take months of planning and building before the big day!

quests.instruction: "A parade route swept clean, its banners lit by a few string lights" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when string lights would actually be needed to see the banners.
quests.explanation: Yes! String lights are needed to see clearly once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: Cleanup crews often work quickly after a parade to get streets ready for regular traffic again!
